targets.title: Genetic predisposition for immune system, hormone, and metabolic dysfunction in myalgic encephalomyelitis/chronic fatigue syndrome: a pilot study.
targets.evidence_quote: We reanalyzed the frequency ratio of the highly prevalent snps in CFS from the Perez et al. study to this more appropriate control.
targets.outcome_computational_quote: The new ratios were recalculated for the 23andMe control and for the ALFA control and subsequently compared to the original ratios.
targets.outcome_robustness_quote: The genetic predispositions reported for Chronic Fatigue Syndrome are not supported when reanalyzed with more appropriate control data including those drawn from the same 23andMe pool as the CFS patients. Out of the original 50 genomic positions presented to have the most prevalent deleterious polymorphisms among CFS sufferers, only three remained that met the original study criterion of at least twice as frequent as healthy individuals.
targets.outcome_reasoning: Original CFS patient frequencies are retained and re-analyzed against alternative controls. This directly evaluates robustness of the original aggregate data; it does not attempt to regenerate the original numbers using the original control workflow. The original risk findings largely disappear under the alternative control constructions.
